summary: A Knightscope security robot patrolling a California park did not respond when a bystander pressed its emergency button during a fight. The button routed calls to the company rather than to police, and a woman injured in the fight needed hospital treatment.
technical_summary: An autonomous K5 security robot with an emergency alert button that was not yet connected to police dispatch. Pressing the button produced a step-out-of-the-way prompt and the robot kept patrolling. Officers arrived about 15 minutes after the fight had ended, so the robot gave no assistance.
systems: Knightscope K5 (HP RoboCop) autonomous security robot

sector.quote: has been patrolling Salt Lake Park for the Huntington Park Police Department

technology.quote: one of more than 70 autonomous security robots developed by Knightscope

failure_mode.quote: It’s a new program for us and were still developing some protocols

notes: The injury came from the fight itself; coded minor because the robot's unconnected alert delayed outside help. Whether the robot itself would have changed the outcome is unclear.

summary: A Dutch tax authority algorithm used to screen childcare benefit claims wrongly labeled tens of thousands of families as fraudsters. Many affected families had lower incomes or immigrant backgrounds, and they were forced to repay money they did not owe.
technical_summary: A self-learning risk-scoring model, deployed from 2013, vetted childcare benefit claims for fraud and treated not holding Dutch citizenship as a risk factor. Civil servants largely rubber-stamped its high-risk flags, producing repayment demands. The model was an opaque black box, offered little explanation, and gave families no meaningful route to contest it.

failure_mode.quote: The model saw not being a Dutch citizen as a risk factor.
it was an opaque black box, with no transparency into its inner workings

harm_type.quote: Forced to pay back money they didn’t owe, many families were driven to financial ruin

Others were left with lasting mental health issues

summary: A Turkish-made Kargu-2 attack drone, reportedly used by forces backing Libya's Tripoli government, may have engaged retreating fighters in 2020 without a live operator link, according to a UN panel. The report does not say whether anyone was killed or injured.
technical_summary: A loitering attack drone that can be operated manually or autonomously and was reportedly programmed to attack targets without a data link to its operator. Per the UN report, retreating fighters were hunted down and remotely engaged by unmanned combat aerial vehicles and loitering munitions. Casualties were not reported.

notes: Casualties are unknown per the excerpts; severity is inferred from the reported attacks on fighters, not from confirmed injuries. Whether a human kept control at the point of attack is disputed.

summary: A widely used health-risk algorithm developed by Optum, used at a large academic hospital, scored Black patients as less in need of extra care than equally sick white patients. Because it predicted future costs rather than health needs, fewer Black patients were enrolled in complex-care programs.
technical_summary: A risk-score model used to select patients for extra care programs. It predicted future health-care costs as a proxy for need, and because Black patients incurred lower costs at the same disease burden, they were scored as lower risk. Race was excluded as an input, but the cost proxy carried racial disparities into enrollment decisions.

summary: Several AI-powered website accessibility overlay vendors allegedly claimed their products would deliver automated compliance with accessibility standards. Critics say those claims were false, leaving customers exposed to legal risk and disabled users still facing barriers.
technical_summary: Third-party JavaScript overlays that were marketed as automatically making websites accessible and compliant with WCAG standards. Critics argue that overlays cannot correct underlying site code, so the claimed compliance and accessibility gains did not hold up for people using assistive technologies.
systems: AI accessibility overlay products (accessiBe, UserWay, Allyable, Accessus.ai, MaxAccess.io)

harm_type.quote: False claims at the expense of customers and persons with disabilities.

affected_population.quote: False claims at the expense of customers and persons with disabilities.

notes: Source is an advocacy site making allegations; the vendors' responses are not in the excerpt. The failure is mainly deceptive marketing, so the mechanism tags are inferred and the AI-technology tag is weakly supported.

summary: A driver using Tesla's Autopilot driver-assistance system ran a red light at high speed and struck a car, killing two people in Gardena, California, in 2019. Prosecutors charged the driver with vehicular manslaughter, reportedly the first felony case of its kind in the United States.
technical_summary: A Tesla Model S with Autopilot, a partial driving-automation system that controls steering, speed and braking, was driving at about 74 mph. Crash data reportedly showed no brakes were used in the six minutes before impact. The system requires an attentive driver, and the case centers on the driver's supervision.

summary: According to former employees, ByteDance scraped videos and profiles from Instagram and Snapchat without consent and reposted them on the Flipagram app around 2017. The content was reportedly used to help train the For You recommendation algorithm for US users.
technical_summary: Automated crawlers reportedly harvested short videos, usernames, profile pictures and descriptions from other platforms and created duplicate accounts on Flipagram, a TikTok predecessor. The scraped data was allegedly used to train the For You personalization algorithm on US content. Allegations rest on anonymous former employees and internal documents.

summary: A Facebook News Feed ranking bug reportedly ran for about six months, causing posts that should have been demoted, including repeat misinformation, to be boosted. The company says the bug had no meaningful long-term impact on its metrics and has been fixed.
technical_summary: A software bug in the News Feed ranking system failed to apply downranking to flagged posts, including content from repeat misinformation offenders and some nudity, violence and state media. Engineers could not find the root cause and watched intermittent spikes until the bug was fixed in March.

summary: DHS software called ATLAS reportedly scans immigration records and can flag naturalized citizens for possible denaturalization under secret criteria. Documents obtained through FOIA show it draws on poorly managed databases, and advocates warn it may produce unfair results.
technical_summary: A USCIS and DHS fraud-screening system that runs on cloud servers, mining federal databases and biometric data for derogatory information. It flags cases for potential fraud or security threats and can consider race, ethnicity and national origin in certain circumstances. Humans make the final determinations, but flags drive the workflow.
